claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 normally forms several primary crystalline phases during conventional solidification.
A short isothermal hold just below the onset of primary crystallization immediately after rapid cooling can suppress primary non-eutectic crystalline-phase formation.
The post-quench isothermal hold can increase amorphous retention.
The post-quench isothermal hold can enhance thermal stability during subsequent slower cooling and reheating.
Rapid quenching produces a largely amorphous state in this alloy.
The relevant hold temperature is within the supercooled-liquid region and approximately 10–20 °C below the crystallization-onset temperature.
The isothermal hold reduces the density of critical crystalline nuclei.
The isothermal hold promotes atomic-level structural relaxation without crossing the nucleation barrier.
Reduced crystalline-seed density inhibits initiation of the multistep crystallization sequence during reheating.
Suppressing crystalline seeds preserves a metastable amorphous structure and thereby enhances thermal stability.
Relative to standard processing, the intervention will produce fewer or diminished crystallization exotherms during thermal analysis.
Relative to standard processing, the intervention will yield a higher retained amorphous fraction detectable by XRD and microscopy.
Under typical rapid cooling, slower cooling, and reheating, extensive primary crystallization causes poor amorphous retention and a complex multistep crystallization sequence.
Holding too close to the crystallization onset or for too long can promote crystallization rather than suppress it.
A hold that is too short or too far below the relevant temperature range may be ineffective at suppressing nucleation.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that rapid quenching achieves a largely amorphous state, whereas the baseline broadly states that typical rapid cooling produces extensive primary crystallization and poor amorphous retention. The cooling-rate regimes needed to reconcile these descriptions are not specified.
